The port reset code bails out early if the current connect status is
cleared (device disconnected).  If we're issuing a hot reset
also look at the link state before the reset is finished.
Section 10.14.2.6 of the USB 3.0 spec says that when a port enters the
Error state or Resetting state
column2: the port connection bit retains the

column1: value from the previous state.  Therefore we can't trust it until the
reset finishes.  Also
column2: the xHCI spec section 4.19.1.2.5 says software

column1: shall ignore the link state while the port is resetting
an unknown state.
The port state during reset is also unknown for USB 2.0 hubs.  The hub
sends a reset signal by driving the bus into an SE0 state.  This
overwhelms the ""connect"" signal from the device
whether anything is connected or not.
Fix the port reset code to ignore the port link state and current
connect bit until the reset finishes
cleared.
Remove the check for USB_PORT_STAT_C_BH_RESET in the warm reset case
because it's redundant.  When the warm reset finishes
bit will be cleared at the same time USB_PORT_STAT_C_BH_RESET is set.
Remove the now-redundant check for a cleared USB_PORT_STAT_RESET bit
in the code to deal with the finished reset.
This patch should be backported to all stable kernels.
